preamble: Bicuspid Aortic Valve  |  100-Point Adverse Prognostic Score  |  ACC/AHA 2021 BAV Guidelines / ESC 2021 VHD  |  Progression Trajectory: Fast / Moderate / Slow

questions.question: Is peak aortic jet velocity ≥4.0 m/s (severe AS) or mean gradient ≥40 mmHg on Doppler echo?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — severe AS confirmed (Vmax ≥4.0 m/s or mean gradient ≥40 mmHg)

questions.question: Is aortic regurgitation severe (vena contracta >6 mm, regurgitant fraction >50%, or LVEDD >65 mm)?
Is aortic root or ascending aorta ≥4.5 cm (adults) or Z-score ≥4 (pediatric) on echo or CT/MRI?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — aortic dilation at or above surgical threshold

questions.question: Has aortic diameter increased ≥0.5 cm/year on serial imaging over ≥2 measurement intervals?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — rapid growth confirmed; surgical repair indicated regardless of absolute size

questions.question: Does CT/MRI show aortic arch or descending aorta involvement beyond the sino-tubular junction?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — pan-aortic disease phenotype; annual full-aorta imaging required

questions.question: Is LVEF <50% on echo or cardiac MRI (systolic dysfunction)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — LV systolic dysfunction confirmed; Class I surgical indication

questions.question: Is LV mass index >115 g/m² (men) / >95 g/m² (women) or septal thickness >13 mm on echo?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — significant LVH confirmed; pressure overload from AS

questions.question: Is there Grade II or III diastolic dysfunction (E/e' ratio >14, LA dilation, elevated filling pressures)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — elevated LV filling pressures confirmed

questions.question: Is there confirmed Turner syndrome (45,X), Loeys-Dietz, or ACTA2/MYH11/TGFBR1/2 pathogenic variant?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — high-risk connective tissue syndrome; lower surgical threshold applies

questions.question: Is there a first-degree relative with aortic dissection, aneurysm ≥5 cm, or confirmed BAV?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — familial BAV or dissection history confirmed

questions.question: Is there a confirmed or repaired coarctation of the aorta (gradient >20 mmHg or prior repair)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — BAV + CoA co-occurrence; higher risk of LV dysfunction and hypertension

questions.question: Is the patient symptomatic from BAV disease (NYHA Class II–IV dyspnea, angina, or syncope)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — symptoms present; Class I trigger for surgical intervention

questions.question: Does exercise testing show reduced functional capacity (<80% predicted METs) or abnormal BP response?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — reduced exercise capacity confirms symptomatic reclassification

questions.question: Is there a prior episode of infective endocarditis on the BAV?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — prior IE confirmed; accelerated valvular destruction risk

questions.question: Has the patient had prior balloon valvuloplasty, surgical AVR, or TAVI?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — structural valve deterioration or prosthesis mismatch risk
